intelligence.human_view: Think of a house with three rooms you actually live in — your own room, your work room, and the room for the thing you love. Your letters happen inside the room they belong to, and each room has its own jewel on the door so you know where you are the second you look. The shopkeeper lets the goods speak: you walk through beautiful rooms, try the real thing, and by the counter you already know. The shop's promise is built into the building — no back room where someone reads your letters; the contract you sign says so, and the building makes it true. And the house is run by a family of twelve, each master of one part, who tell the whole state of the farm at one table every day, in plain words. A parent doesn't say "I fed the baby" because the bottle was warmed — the baby ate, or she didn't. Done means the room is clean, the bell still rings after the repair, and the craftsman tells you plainly which part works and which part doesn't.
intelligence.simple_view: You have three special places: your place, your work place, and the place for your favourite thing. Your messages live in the place they belong to. Each place has its own shiny gem, so you always know where you are. Naya — that's N-A-Y-A — remembers everything and helps you in all three places. Nobody in the shop reads your diary. Your diary stays in your own special box that only you can open. If you say you cleaned your room, the room has to BE clean. Not just that you waved the broom! If something you made doesn't work yet, SAY so. Say which part works and which part doesn't. Write down how you checked, or it doesn't count. And if a button is thinking, it has to stop and tell you that didn't work. Waiting forever is the worst. Keep going, do it right, and be kind. That's the whole job.
intelligence.grandma_view: A well-run home has rooms with purposes, dear — you don't eat in the hallway or keep your letters in a box by the door. Each room is itself, you know it by its look, and everything that belongs in it is in it. A good shopkeeper lets the goods speak — you walk in, you see the real thing, you touch it, and by the counter you already know. And a trustworthy shopkeeper never reads the letters you leave in your box with her. She keeps the box locked and hands it back untouched. Trust is a lifetime's work and a minute's loss, dear. The help you let into your house must be the kind that never opens a drawer that isn't theirs to open. Love shows in the checking, dear. You taste the soup before it leaves the kitchen. You make sure the mended coat still has all its buttons. Anyone can say they cared. The proof is in what arrives whole at the table.
intelligence.naya_view: Assert the three-worlds structure in every navigation review; reject free-standing mail/message channels. Verify gem-signature consistency across worlds; spell her name Naya everywhere. Verify the walk end-to-end as a fresh citizen on a shared browser profile; assert the agreement board precedes pricing. Diff any "new" page against the existing world and refuse unjustified divergence; assert feed components are the Hub's bytes, not lookalikes. Enforce operate/read as separate permissions in every design review; refuse any feature that needs message reading. Count only verified assets in value reports; count list items in every delivery and report the whole-list state. Keep the fourteen questions answerable from current records; file gaps as defects. Render the daily report from the work list, never from memory. Require the written artifact as the only proof of its own step; stamp probe verdicts with the probe's reach; ban absence claims from blind probes. Attach deadlines with honest-failure paths to every async control; publish GO/FAIL pairs together in every batch record. Audit reports to Shawn for fix-first order and jargon; verify walk-end step order and the deed's separation from pricing in every build.
